title: Crispi Corn Tortilla Bowls with Lime-Poached Cod
description: Soft corn tortillas and cabbage braise in the Crispi while flaky cod poaches gently for a taco bowl with lime gravy.
equipment: Ninja Crispi PowerPod with US Bake preset
Butter knife or fork for checking fish

ingredients.name: skinless boneless cod
ingredients.note: Fully thawed, pin bones removed; cut across the loin into portions no thicker than 1/2 inch.

ingredients.name: soft corn tortillas
ingredients.note: Small plain tortillas, about 5 inches across; cut into short narrow ribbons.

ingredients.name: green cabbage
ingredients.note: Remove the core and thick ribs; shred very finely, then cut into short shreds.

ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken broth
ingredients.note: Choose plain meat-and-bone broth without a vegetable blend.

steps.title: Set up the Crispi
steps.text: Use the room-temperature 6-cup Crispi glass container without an adapter. Leave out the crisper plate so the food sits in liquid. Load the container before starting the PowerPod and keep the storage lid off during cooking.

steps.title: Moisten the tortilla base
steps.text: Toss {tortillas}, {cabbage} and {ancho} with one quarter of {broth} in the unheated glass. Press the ribbons down into the liquid.

steps.title: Braise the cabbage
steps.text: Seat the PowerPod and select Bake for 10 minutes. Fold the top ribbons into the moist center with a silicone spoon. Cook in 2–3 minute intervals until the cabbage crushes easily and the tortillas are softened, about 12–20 minutes total.

steps.title: Set the poaching temperature
steps.text: Meanwhile heat the remaining {broth} in the HexClad to 140°F, checking the liquid with a thermometer. Adjust the burner to maintain the poaching liquid at 139–140°F.

steps.title: Poach the cod
steps.text: Lay {cod} in the broth in one layer. Keep the pan covered between thermometer checks and maintain the liquid at 139–140°F, checking every few minutes. Allow about 12–25 minutes for the thickest centers to reach 138–140°F.

steps.title: Check the flake
steps.text: Check each thickest center: it must be opaque throughout and flake easily with a fork. If it is still translucent or sticks together, continue in the 139–140°F liquid, rechecking every 2 minutes. Transfer cooked portions to warm plates with a spoonful of broth.

steps.title: Measure the gravy
steps.text: Strain the poaching broth and return about 1/2 cup per serving to the HexClad. Bring it to a full boil.

steps.title: Mix the slurry
steps.text: Stir {starch} into {water} in a small cup until smooth.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Whisk the freshly stirred slurry into the simmering sauce and stir for 1 minute, until it coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Finish the lime gravy
steps.text: Whisk {crema} and {lime} into the gravy off heat until smooth.

steps.title: Assemble the bowls
steps.text: Divide the soft tortilla mixture between two bowls. Place the cod on top in moist flakes and coat generously with gravy.

notes: Make ahead: Cut the cabbage and tortilla ribbons ahead. Keep the ribbons dry until cooking and poach the fish just before serving. Option A uses lime and mild ancho. For gentler Option B, omit both and add finely minced parsley to the gravy. For dairy-free sauce omit the cream cheese. Refrigerate promptly in shallow portions and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: No. The softened tortillas lose their shape when frozen and the thin cod flakes can firm up after reheating. Fridge reheat: Warm a single portion with its sauce in a covered HexClad skillet over medium-low, adding a splash of water if thick. Stir or turn gently and begin checking after 5 minutes. Heat the cod to 165°F throughout. Freezer reheat: If already frozen, thaw overnight in the refrigerator and follow the fridge reheating directions. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/2 of recipe): 206 kcal, 26.7 g protein, 16.6 g total carbohydrate, 3.3 g fat, 2.1 g fiber, 137 mg sodium. Includes the measured broth and sauce. Sodium varies with your broth.
